notes.title: Earth Analog v2.0 - Biggest update so far!
notes.content:
Greetings, Deep Space Explorers!

We’re thrilled to announce the launch of Earth Analog v2.0 - the first major update to the game!

This update brings game-changing new features, along with a host of improvements based on your valuable feedback. [b]We've tackled many of the known issues and refined the experience to make your journey through the mysterious deep space even more immersive.[/b]

Here’s a look at the most significant changes:

[h1]New Features[/h1]

[h3]Refined Flight Mechanics[/h3]
This update introduces a simplified, streamlined control system, a new auto-leveling feature, and a reworked throttle that replaces Full Thrust mode - all designed to make planetary flight smoother, more intuitive, and more relaxing.

[h3]Planetary System Study[/h3]
The Knowledge system has been replaced with an all-new gameplay mechanic centered around conducting scientific research on exoplanets. Complete tasks such as scanning alien vegetation, analyzing samples in your onboard lab, or deploying atmospheric probes to uncover system secrets and earn Expedition Points. These points can be used to upgrade your ship or unlock new star sectors for exploration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/679c696a9b22c7125c33e5978d0b39b50412080b.png[/img]

[h3]Base Building[/h3]
A brick-based building system allows players to construct bases, outposts, etc. Advanced building techniques like [i]SNOT[/i] (Studs Not On Top) construction are fully supported! You’ll be able to construct bases with teleporters to travel quickly between them. Imagine building a home on a distant planet, in another dimension...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/1627cf10a423d16c5c4d88023bf08cb3637dbac9.jpg[/img]

[h3]Online Discovery Database[/h3]
Tracks and log planetary discoveries - be the first to leave your mark on the universe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/0380f50e08e7b6a47492c271f72124421d77e3ba.jpg[/img]

[h3]New Dark Energy Gameplay[/h3]
Dark energy will now appear in pockets you’ll need to fly through, demanding more skill and making flight feel more rewarding.

[h3]Enhanced Radio Scanner[/h3]
Now a key tool for planetary analysis and discovery.

[h3]New Ship Upgrades[/h3]
Earn Expedition Points to upgrade your ship at pylons, with 50+ new ship systems and upgrades available. You can now also upgrade non-ship systems, like your jet pack.

[h3]Improved Onboarding[/h3]
The tutorial has been replaced by a "learn as you play" system making onboarding an enjoyable experience.

[h3]Volumetric Clouds[/h3]
Stunning volumetric clouds bring even more depth and realism to the alien skies.

[h3]Polygonal Rendering[/h3]
The game’s unique rendering engine now supports polygon meshes, bringing enhanced detail to vegetation, ships, and constructs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/cea8a909d1186137e3d526f7c3d032d59f067c99.png[/img]

[h3]4K Visual & UI Overhaul[/h3]
Textures are now optimized for 4K resolution, delivering sharper visuals. The user interface has seen numerous improvements - for example, the onboard computer now displays in fullscreen mode for better usability.

===

If you're enjoying the new changes and improvements, please consider updating your Steam review - it really helps support the game and its future development!
Many thanks!

nkm
Funcraft Games

[b]Full change log:[/b]
[list]
[*] new: construction system based on bricks. Allows for base/factory construction and ship construction.
[*] new: gameplay mechanic: planetary system study. Complete study tasks to deliver a final assessment of the system.
[*] new: advanced ship and non-ship (e.g. jetpack) upgrades. Upgrades can now be purchased freely with Expedition Points.
[*] new: laboratory: analyze stones and artifacts under your ownboard microscope to boost their value and uncover their past and secrets.
[*] new: flight mechanics: auto-leveling feature & reworked throttle. Flying has been made easier and smoother in general.
[*] new: UI has been completely overhauled to make it more accessible and appealing.
[*] new: volumetric clouds.
[*] new: planetary vegeration.
[*] new: factory buildings, like a Water Extractor, allow you to automate resource gathering.
[*] new: online discovery database. Tracks and logs planetary discoveries. Be the first to discover a planet!
[*] new: jetpack rocket vault upgrade: launch over long distances with a powerful jump rocket.
[*] new: HUD icons.
[*] new: rich sediment item. May contain interesting items to be found with analysis.
[*] new: sample nexus POI, a location rich of rich sediment items.
[*] new: QoL: tooltips and notifications.
[*] new: Steam leaderboard.
[*] new: additional achievements.
[*] changed: reduced the number of controls, e.g. removed all the ship computer controls.
[*] changed: ship computer interaction is now full screen and with mouse interaction support.
[*] changed: dark energy is now collected in small pockets.
[*] changed: radio scanner now scans in sweeps and adds directional information to make finding easier.
[*] changed: all textures have been upscaled to 4k resolutions.
[*] changed: all mini-games (drilling, repairing, etc) have been overhauled.
[*] changed: improved variety of procedurally generated planetary systems.
[*] changed: map now shows additional information per system.
[*] changed: parallax bump mapping: improved texture details up close.
[*] removed: tutorial, replaced with a learn-as-you-play system.
[*] removed: modding support.
[*] removed: non-english locales. Will be re-added later.
[/list]

notes.title: Exciting v2.0 Update: Playtest Launch and What to Expect!
notes.content:
Hello deep space explorers,

Here's an update on the upcoming free EA update! Plus, a question: [i]who’s interested in playtesting the first two planetary systems of the new update and provide us with feedback?[/i] DM me if you're in (or reply to this announcement): your feedback will shape this game.

Progress on the next update is moving along smoothly and steadily. There are so many changes that we've decided to call it v2.0! :)

Here’s a breakdown of the key changes you can look forward to:

[list]
[*] [b]v2.0 will emphasize your role as a deep space explorer/scientist.[/b] A new gameplay mechanic called the "Planetary System Study" will be introduced, where you must complete study tasks to deliver a final assessment of the system. Tasks could include things like “find and scan this plant species” or “build an atmospheric probe to analyze the atmosphere.” Each completed task reveals more about the planetary system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/679c696a9b22c7125c33e5978d0b39b50412080b.png[/img]

[*] [b]v2.0 extends EA's unique ray marching engine with polygon meshes.[/b] The polygons will be used to render details like vegetation, your ship, and other constructs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/cea8a909d1186137e3d526f7c3d032d59f067c99.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/6dc29279d77c6c52c001a7e0ccff025e2c6c49ea.png[/img]

[*] [b]v2.0 introduces a building system [/b]inspired by a famous Danish toy brand, allowing you to build pretty much anything. Yes, even SNOT construction is possible (the building experts know what I mean :) ). You’ll be able to construct bases with teleporters to travel quickly between them. Imagine building a home on a distant planet in another dimension...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/b872fdff8a55b0e6217c385fb6ce189c68d04c1d.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/d8c992b2a17c3e38b404f94a74cb8f75fd90ccbc.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/ccc6111914f5fd5cf0f02b0e71cd300da41c0ae0.png[/img]

[*] [b]The flight model has been tweaked[/b]—e.g. an auto-leveling system now keeps your roll aligned with the horizon. Full Thrust mode is gone, replaced with a more precise throttle.

[*] [b]Flight controls have been simplified and streamlined.[/b] Fewer controls are now needed for standard flight actions, and all redundant control mappings have been removed.

[*] [b]Dark energy will now appear in pockets you’ll need to fly through[/b], demanding more skill and making flight feel more rewarding.

[*] [b]Greater focus will be placed on the Radio Scanner[/b], which has become more refined.

[*] [b]You can now freely upgrade your ship by spending [i]Expedition Points[/i][/b], earned by selling stones or artifacts to pylons. The number of ship systems and upgrades has been greatly expanded—there are now 50 in total, with more planned.

[*] [b]The UI, HUD, and ship computer have been completely overhauled[/b] for a better user experience.

[*] [b]The tutorial has been removed[/b], replaced with a “learn as you play” system.

[*] [b]Textures and images have been upgraded to 4K[/b], delivering sharper detail and higher visual fidelity.
[/list]

...and much more!

When can you expect the next update? That largely depends on the results of the playtest. If the new game mechanics prove to be fun in their current form, we’re aiming for a release by Q2 next year.

I hope you're as excited for v2.0 as we are! Thanks for your time, and see you soon.
nkm

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/17c4ff65a74d816ac1f59034feb1cfa1fd203115.png[/img]

notes.title: News on the next big 1.2 update
notes.content:
Hello explorers,

It's been a while since the last news bit on Earth Analog but rest assured: I'm still around and have been working hard on the next big (free) update: [b]1.2[/b]. which is expected Q1 2022!

Here follows an overview of the key features of the upcoming 1.2 update.

[h1]Procedurally generated galaxy[/h1]
In addition to the existing planets of the game's linear quest the v1.2 update will introduce a fully procedurally generated galaxy consisting of randomly generated planetary systems. Discover thousands of unique systems on your way to a supermassive black hole. Go where you please and explore at your own pace.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/234b78d2ef8e934974db286e7cf63152cb7d0ae4.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/37e9edbe97b735017b39d26fd51788ae4df1f452.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/c6be01fed423c016a915fb45ca1fb2798564990e.jpg[/img]

[h1]Disembark[/h1]
Disembark your spaceship and explore the fractal planets on foot. This adds whole new level of immersion to the game. Visit exoplanetary beaches, dynamic mountain ranges, living craters, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/2222559fd94ca4aeb715445a98fbf9a9d095ea29.jpg[/img]

[h1]Knowledge System[/h1]
Collect data samples  and complete knowledge studies to unlock new star sectors.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/bfcc0fdd13b1ccad127ab14ea58282bd35f322c8.jpg[/img]

[h1]Autoland[/h1]
With autoland, landing will become a quick routine. Flight in general will be easier in 1.2.

[h1]Improved planetary tech[/h1]
The update will add many new phenomena, like binary and ternary star systems,  different class stars, gas giants, weather, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/f30815a5edce60a29117db8af3f8b13ddba426dd.jpg[/img]

1.2 will also bring a revamped UI, improved controls and many small improvements and tweaks.

This concludes the sneak peek at the upcoming 1.2. I'm very excited about this update and I hope you will be too. If you have any questions please post them below!

Cheers,

notes.title: Freedom Update released!
notes.content:
Hello deep space explorers,

The first major update of the game - called the Freedom Update - it out! This following video highlights the biggest new features:

[previewyoutube=z36oAZoES-E;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Free Roaming[/h1]

With 1.1 the game takes its first big step towards a more free-form/non-linear type of game, i.e. a game in which the quest is not mandatory and in which you have the freedom to go wherever you want to go, right from the start. 

Most planetary systems will be unlocked when you start the game. Some will still remain hidden behind pylons or quest objectives.

[h1]Seamless Experience[/h1]

No more loading fade-to-blacks during cryo jumps: in 1.1 the game only loads and generates assets once (at startup) allowing for a seamless, more realistic experience while playing.
Note that loading can take some time the first time.

[h1]Radio Scanner[/h1]

Beacon signals are no longer be picked up automatically. Instead you will have to use the Radio Scanner to detect the radio waves transmitted by the beacons. Same holds for other radio wave transmitters, like pylons, crystals, portals etc. What else is hidden within the radio spectrum...?

[h1]Dark Energy Overhaul[/h1]

In 1.1 dark energy is no longer be accumulated. Instead the amount of dark energy that can be used for boosting is be based on the strength of the dark energy field at the ship's location. Most often this means that you will be able to boost more when you are closer to the surface. Risk vs. reward.

[h1]Mod Kit[/h1]

A lot of effort has been put in making the game mod friendly. In 1.1 anyone with some lua and GLSL experience is able to expand the galaxy by adding planetary systems of their own creation. The planetary looks and physics are defined by the GLSL shaders and the planetary behavior is defined by the lua script. 

The mod kit includes an example system ([i]Antar a[/i]) of a ring planet harboring a moving crater controlled by tidal forces from a nearby moon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/33d5411ff3e7da47f356a8bbf5977618ea6fc4d9.png[/img]

[h1]And more[/h1]

The update also adds Quality-of-Life improvements, like a scalable UI to accommodate high res monitors. The tutorial has also been improved. Gameplay has been balanced with the removal of cluttering mechanics like Dismantle and Quick FIx.

[h1]Full patch notes[/h1]
[list]
[*] new: free roaming.
[*] new: radio scanner.
[*] new: mod kit.
[*] new: automatic UI upscaling at resolutions higher than 1920x1080.
[*] new: droplets fx, dirt fx.
[*] new: auto exposure.
[*] new: Points-of-interests which are behind celestial bodies are now shown dimmed.
[*] changed: dark energy (DE) mechanic: DE does not accumulate anymore. Now, the strength of the DE determines the DE boost speed directly. The more DE there is at a partical spot, the higher the boost speed.
[*] changed: one does not need to be close to the terrain anymore to be able to use the Dimension Device.
[*] changed: limited max telescope zoom factor to 10x.
[*] changed: lowered fuel and water consumption by 25%.
[*] changed: drilling will now always yield a base amount of resource.
[*] changed: reduced default keyb/mouse roll rate to 75%.
[*] changed: drill screen shows resource intensity in its specific color.
[*] removed: Dismantle mechanic.
[*] removed: Quick Fix. Full Fix is now called Repair.
[*] removed: planet verdict.
[*] removed: message when picking up another crystal.
[*] fixed: jump event issue that caused a non-existing upgrade to be given.
[*] fixed: impact alerts were given for artifacts, portals and crystals.
[*] fixed: issue with the mouse cursor after loading causing wild ship rotations.
[*] fixed: missing Windows taskbar and task manager icons.
[*] fixed: sometimes sending out the probe would damage the hull.
[*] fixed: the probe could be sent out when the Surface resource was selected.
[*] fixed: fog issue on GJ 669b causing the planet to turn red when viewed from far away.
[*] fixed: pressing ENTER to reset the computer alarm would sometimes unintentionally activate the dimension device or start a scan.
[*] fixed: gravity issues on Ryker and Neutron Star.
[*] fixed: various minor UI issues.
[/list]

Stay tuned for more updates!

Best regards,
nkm

notes.title: Earth Analog released!
notes.content:
[h1]Finally![/h1]

After 3 years of hard work, we're happy to bring you the news that Earth Analog has been [b]released[/b]! ːsteamhappyː

In Earth Analog, a space-flight adventure game based on mathematical functions called [i]fractals[/i], you take control of the exploration vessel Eurisko XI in a quest through deep space. Your goal: find our new home.  

Earth Analog is mostly a relaxing game, with the occasional tense moment. You start the game orbiting Proxima Centauri b, a conventional and familiar planet in some ways. But as you travel deeper into space you'll discover ever so stranger worlds... can you survive in your "tin can"?

[b]Reminder: the game is very GPU-heavy due to its raymarching-based rendering, so you need a strong GPU to be able to play at acceptable frame rates. Make sure your system meets the minimal requirements to avoid disappointments.[/b]

We hope you'll enjoy the game! If you have any feedback, please let us know in the forums! We appreciate any feedback that allows us to improve the game!

Regards,
nkm / Funcraft Games

P.S. the game does not come with shrooms included ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Development Update #2
notes.content:
Hello explorers,

[b]Good news:[/b] the main storyline of the game is done and the most game-systems are in place! We're perfectly on track for the Q1 2021 release.

We're currently deep in the polishing phase, that means, polishing the story (with the help of esteemed sci fi-writer Jack Nilssen, go read his books ːsteamhappyː), polishing the gameplay (ensuring it is a fun and gratifying experience), making the graphics even more awesome, optimizing for performance and handling playtester feedback.

A lot of things have changed since the last Development Update. For instance, we ditched the Task System in favor for a more metroidvania-like progression system and both the mentioned artifact and probe systems have gone through many iterations since. We've also made the cockpit a bit sexier:

That's it for now! Stay tuned for more updates.

notes.title: Development Update
notes.content:
Hello explorers,

I wanted to give you a brief update on the development of the game and explain some of the new game mechanics.

The game is currently roughly [b]30%[/b] complete. The first act of the story is done, which includes a dozen handcrafted planets to explore as well as the first procedurally generated arid planet. The final game will have a combination of both hand crafted and procedural planets. The story/quest takes place on the hand crafted planets while the procedural planets are mostly for finding important resources (like water for living, helium for fuel and iron for maintenance) and [b]rare objects[/b].

The following screenshot shows a planet generated by the procedural generator. It's a planet in the Gezebe system.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/2a5ba553a3d6096b452b97c1c82cd2eff4dd7431.png[/img]

The game now features a [b]task system[/b]. As a science/exploration vessel you will often be busy carrying out tasks which contribute to the acquisition of scientific data. For instance, scanning and drilling for water in underground caves systems, or mapping the planet surface. The collected data is used to compile a planet report, which includes a verdict on whether the planet is an Earth Analog or not. Completing tasks also grants you Upgrade Points (ups) that allow you to upgrade ship systems.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/e2c4350f71119e297b592966e3fcd848ad0294e0.png[/img]

Another new and important part of the game is about [b] hunting down rare objects[/b] like stones and alloy-based items. These objects can be used to unlock far-away star systems or can be exchanged for upgrade points. 

Obtaining a specific alloy-based object usually involves: 
[olist]
[*] determining a candidate planet based on planet properties, like climate, and traveling to this planet.
[*] flying through the terrain while scanning for traces of alloys using the ship's broad forward scanner and optional alloy proximity scanner.
[*] using the ship's depth scanner to exactly pinpoint the object location underneath the planet surface.
[*] drilling at that location to excavate the object.
[/olist]
Later in the game you will unlock [b]probe[/b] tech. The probe can help you finding objects and resources.

⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36349490/866894003e2e41b6990ee77703aff662f18baa0b.gif[/img]


[b]Playtesters needed[/b]

I've decided that before I start working on act two (of three total) of the game I first need player feedback on the first part of the game. I'm in need for a serious playtester who is truly willing to play through a chunk of the game and give honest and constructive feedback. In exchange he/she will be able to play the game as one of the first, have a strong influence on how the game will become and get to name one of the game's planets (as well as get an official mention in the credits). 

If you're interested in playtesting please send an email to: info@funcraft-games.net. Please note that the game is based on raymarching tech and therefore requires a powerful gpu to run smoothly. 

Cheers,
nkm
